protectedEffects: TWO OWNER-APPROVED LOCAL INSTALLATIONS, each of a SHA-256-pinned MSI under its own explicit gate: the 3d5a90e release, then the cab71a5 re-cut that replaced it. No production, deployment, database mutation, external send, payment, credential access or secret storage.
notes: AUTHORING BASIS. Hand-authored under a one-time Phase 5 exception, because ProjectOS contains readers for .projectops/closure/<PHASE>.json but no writer: closureGate.ts builds the path and reads it twice, phase.ts writes only the phase record via savePhase, and a repository-wide search finds only path builders, readers and a decisions parser. Phase 4 set the same precedent in commit 0b441a8. The exception is limited to this phase and is not standing. An official `projectos evidence record` command is carry-forward.

WHY THE SUBJECT MOVED, AND WHAT THAT COST. The first release was cut at 3d5a90e and proven live. The owner-accepted-HIGH correction to G4-10 then landed as cab71a5, changing 7 source files AFTER that subject. G4-12 correctly declared the 3d5a90e evidence STALE: it permits a later head only when everything between subject and head is closure-tail metadata, and cab71a5 is substantive source. Rebinding the evidence to cab71a5 without rebuilding was REFUSED by the owner, because it would have decoupled the proof from the bytes that were actually installed. The truthful resolution was a full re-cut: new subject, new owner signature, new MSI, new installation, new headed proof — all at cab71a5. Nothing was weakened to avoid the work.

Canonical subject 713 bytes, sha256 97f6c6790e00dfec6f5d6313cb67c1cbb58ecbb82f7c70bcb64a119570bd472f, generated twice byte-identically. buildId cab71a5dfd63 and daemonArtefact.buildId cab71a5dfd63. Dependency closure CLOSED (2 files). MSI ddbc7d995663d7884d824a797dc602b08e4fae647922607f840cc7dfade12df5, 37,224,448 bytes, ProductCode {88893E5E-0AB9-4DA7-A6D8-A74967DC2622}, UpgradeCode {E0D5D7AF-3631-53BF-9085-BE20BB8B99F7}, x64, per-machine, InstallerVersion 500. OWNER SIGNATURE. Verified with Node's OpenSSL against the public point read out of the PRODUCTION half of anchor.rs, never against a key handed to a verifier. 128 lowercase hex characters, no trailing newline, 64 decoded raw r||s bytes, es256, key projectos-signing-20260812. Four negative controls all rejected: one flipped subject bit, one flipped signature bit, the signature read as DER instead of P1363, and — the control that proves the re-cut is real — the earlier 3d5a90e signature, which does NOT verify this subject. The anchor is byte-identical between 3d5a90e and cab71a5, so no trust anchor moved.

SUBJECT-BOUND VALIDATOR RUN, G4-17. .projectops/validation/cab71a5dfd63e22c9c0b0ee23609f2245d5eb81a.json, 14,154 bytes, sha256 21d6b9f169cd316f2669017610e63a3b165a86d2d9ea2d38d616b2042cb872e0. Written by validate-all --record-evidence from a CLEAN tree at this exact commit inside the isolated release worktree: 129 registered modules, 129 PASS, 0 FAIL, exit 0, aggregatePassed true, workingTreeCleanAtRunStart true. Copied into this repository byte-identically; both copies hash 21d6b9f1. The plan's required validator for this phase is the aggregate validate-all, and it is recorded passing BY NAME.

A REPOSITORY DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY, AND NOT PAPERED OVER. The first attempt at that record failed 124/129, and the second 125/129. None of the failures was a defect at either commit: this repository has NO .gitattributes and core.autocrlf=true, so a fresh worktree materialises CRLF, and five checks are pinned to LF bytes — a provenance digest over node-v24.14.1-SHASUMS256.txt (2967 LF vs 2999 CRLF), a digest over docs/architecture/projectos-v3-master-plan.md (7bd6235f LF vs 392420ed CRLF), and two validators whose regexes contain a literal \n that cannot match \r\n. A sixth failure, validate-desktop-e2e, only wanted the frontend bundle that the MSI build produces. The affected files were restored to their exact committed blobs — proven byte-identical each time — and nothing was edited, weakened or excluded. A .gitattributes fix is carry-forward, deliberately NOT made during this phase.

THE SIGNATURE IS INDEPENDENT OF LINE ENDINGS, AND THIS WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The daemon bundle contains ZERO CR bytes despite being built from a CRLF checkout in which one source alone carries 429 CRLF pairs and templates.ts bakes 31 into a template literal — esbuild normalises its output. The signed manifest hashes exactly two things, the pinned node.exe and the daemon bundle, both by raw file read, so no document or source text ever enters the subject. Restoring line endings therefore could not, and did not, invalidate the owner's signature.

HEADED PROOF, PERFORMED AGAINST THE INSTALLED cab71a5 BUILD. Installed once, msiexec /qn /norestart, exit 0, no reboot, no pending rename. The same-version major upgrade replaced the 3d5a90e product; exactly ONE product is registered afterwards. Launched from the real Start Menu shortcut as the normal user: MEDIUM integrity, parent explorer.exe, one process, running the exact installed binary. Exactly one daemon, from the packaged runtime, with an explicit --root; its whole environment is three variables including PROJECTOS_GIT_EXE bound to one absolute git.exe (git 2.55.0, Authenticode Valid) and NO PATH, so no other git is resolvable. No development or debug fallback. Owner Control, Owner Chat, Safety and Providers all on live governed truth: plan 1.0 PLAN READY (recomputed), IN EXECUTION, 4 of 6 phases accepted, 66.7%, and Phase 5 correctly shown as AWAITING CLOSURE with 'Closure authority is ChatGPT. The implementer (Claude Code) cannot close a phase.' Owner Chat answered live. Safety showed production frozen, no provider contacted, no secret used, no AI API used, provider guards REFUSED. Objective entry, plan-proposal and activation surfaces present and truthful. Restart and recovery clean: the daemon exited with the app and exactly one returned. Controls keyboard-focusable; nothing material clipped at 1200x820 or at reduced size. A stale-claim sweep across all nine routes found NONE.

THE SIX LIFECYCLE LABELS AND THE STAGE-ONLY NOTE. All six ship in the packaged frontend bundle — Record prompt ready, Move to implementation, Move to validation, Move to evidence, Move to review, Move to closure review — together with the note 'This only changes the recorded phase stage. It does not perform the work or send anything.' None of the six superseded imperatives (Run validation, Collect evidence, Send for review, Begin implementation) appears anywhere in it. Only one label is observable at a time because the label follows phase status. At awaiting_closure the note is correctly ABSENT and no stage button is offered: NEXT_STEP in GovernedActions.tsx deliberately has no entry for awaiting_closure, because the only remaining action is owner-gated closure, not a stage change. That absence is truthful behaviour, not a missing control.

NO GOVERNED STATE WAS CHANGED THROUGH THE UI. No plan was activated and no lifecycle action was pressed — in particular 'Close as ChatGPT', which the installed build offers at this stage, was NOT pressed. The application and its daemon were closed after the proof.

REVIEWS. Code, security, reliability and ECC reviews complete for the release and for the G4-10 correction it carries. The ECC review of this re-cut independently re-derived every hash from the extracted MSI rather than trusting reported figures, and returned 0 CRITICAL. It confirmed the daemon hash change is fully explained by the four non-test changed files reaching the bundle through a static import chain; that the signed manifest covers runtime and daemon only, unchanged in scope; that isolation held; and that main.wxs carries AllowSameVersionUpgrades=yes, which is what makes a same-version re-cut replace rather than duplicate. Its one additional HIGH — that the executable is not byte-reproducible — was REJECTED on verification: the target-directory and MSI-embedded executables differ by exactly three contiguous bytes at offset 0x6bf710, 'UNK' to 'MSI', which is Tauri's own logged bundle-type patch and not compiler entropy. Only one build was performed, so executable reproducibility remains UNTESTED and is claimed neither way.

FINDINGS: 0 CRITICAL, 1 HIGH, 1 unresolved. SR-1 is the executable-attestation finding: the signed ProjectOS trust manifest covers the packaged Node runtime and the daemon bundle but does NOT cover projectos-control-center.exe, and that executable is not Authenticode-signed. 'SIGNED' therefore means runtime and daemon integrity, never end-to-end release integrity. My earlier claim that the buildId carries the source binding for the executable was OVERSTATED and was corrected by review.

SR-1 DISPOSITION. Murad explicitly accepted SR-1 as a residual HIGH for this local operational-recovery closure only. It is NOT fixed, NOT downgraded and NOT withdrawn, and it remains a carry-forward finding. The acceptance grants no production approval, no external-distribution approval, and no claim that the executable is cryptographically attested. It is recorded here as unresolved so the gate must see it: G4-10 will refuse this phase until a committed gatekeeper decision carries the matching owner acceptance, bound to this phase, this subject and this finding id, with scope phase-closure-only.

CARRY-FORWARD, recorded rather than tidied away: SR-1 as above; ProjectOS has no command that writes this evidence record; validate-all cannot be pointed at a subject other than HEAD; the repository has no .gitattributes while core.autocrlf is true, so fresh worktrees are not reproducible without restoration; two validators use \n-only regexes and two checks pin digests over LF bytes; the core package has no test-typecheck while the agent package does; and the duplicate-identity scan in G4-10 is O(n squared), which is not exploitable under this programme's tamperProof:false model but is noted.
